text:
Noah Kim: Heads up from recruiting: candidate asked if they have a qualifying life event (QLE) midyear, can they change 401k deferral immediately or is it only during open enroll? They mentioned a promotion coming that changes pay band.

Sofia Green: Promotions and changes to pay typically allow election changes for 401k deferrals once the HR system reflects the new employee record. BrightPlan supports midyear deferral changes on QLEs but we need the HRIS event tag (promotion) + effective date.

Noah Kim: Ok — what's the minimal paperwork we should collect to trigger that? Recruiting wants a checklist to pass to hiring manager.

Benji Carter: Minimal: 1) Promotion approval email or internal form, 2) effective date, 3) employee confirmation of new deferral % (signed or via BrightPlan). Send to benefits@redwood.com and payroll will process.

BenefitsBot: Note: Midyear deferral switches take effect on the first payroll after processing. Payroll cutoff: changes submitted by Wednesday 12pm PT before payroll week for that cycle.

Noah Kim: Great. Another wrinkle: the candidate also asked whether enrolling in a full FSA immediately disqualifies them from HSA contributions if their HDHP starts same month. We had a case with timing issues last quarter.

Sofia Green: BrightPlan marks the elections but the decisive check is coverage effective dates + plan types. If HDHP effective date and FSA effective date are the same month and FSA is full-purpose, payroll will block HSA pre-tax contributions. If they want HSA, choose limited-purpose FSA or delay FSA start to next month.

Hannah (Payroll): Adding: we can do a manual payroll override to allow temporary HSA contributions if theres documentation showing HDHP start + limited-purpose FSA, but we need benefits approval and the vendor ticket number.

Noah Kim: How do we get that vendor ticket number? BrightPlan support?

Benji Carter: Yes — BrightPlan support creates tickets for enrollment inconsistencies. We also keep a vendor ops contact: support_ops@brightplan.com. If it's urgent tag it "redwood-payroll-impact".

BenefitsBot: FYI: When making manual overrides, payroll records an audit note and requires an employee-signed acknowledgement for tax records.

Sofia Green: Also flag: HSA catch-up contributions (age 55+) are allowed midyear if eligibility criteria met, but again payroll needs the effective date and proof of HDHP. For employees already enrolled in a full FSA, we recommend they switch to limited-purpose FSA before submitting HSA payroll elections.

Noah Kim: Good guidance. Last Q: can we surface the 401k default deferral and match summary directly in offers? Recruiting asked for exact wording so candidates see match timing and vesting.

Benji Carter: Use: "You will be automatically enrolled at 5% pre-tax deferral unless you elect otherwise. Company match: 100% of the first 3% and 50% of the next 2% (maximum company contribution of 4% of pay). Company contributions vest 25% after 12 months of service then monthly to 100% at 48 months."

Noah Kim: Thanks — I'll update the offer templates. Can someone add a short line about rollover acceptance and the BrightPlan rollover form? Candidates keep asking.

Sofia Green: Added to the hiring doc: "We accept trustee-to-trustee rollovers; see BrightPlan rollover form (internal)."

Hannah (Payroll): Final note: if a candidate wants contributions in their first check, recruiting must confirm signed offer + benefits elections and send to payroll 10 business days before start date.

Noah Kim: Perfect. I'll circulate the checklist and new offer language to recruiting. Appreciate the quick responses! :pray:
